page.layout: Two coin medallions centred at the top, with engraved legends; below them one column of text in two paragraphs. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: LYSIMACHVS illustri quidem Macedoniæ loco na-
tus, sed virtutis ornamentis omni nobilitate clarior extitit.hic
animi magnitudine, Philosophia, virium gloria, omnes per
quos Oriens domitus est,vicit. A Callisthene,quamuis trunca-
to auribus, naribus, ac labiis, præcepta Philosophiæ accipere
non erubuit.hunc ferocissimo leoni obiecit Alexander:leonis
linguam hic statim avulsit: chariorem inde habuit eum Ale-
xander,quem imprudens cùm in fronte vulnerasset, diadema
sibi demptum Rex alligandi vulneris causa, capiti eius impo-
suit, quod auspicium primum regalis maiestatis Lysimacho
fuit. Regnavit itaque in Macedonia anno mundi 3676. ante
Christum natum 286. Post mortem Alexandri cùm inter suc-
cessores provinciæ dividerentur, Thraces,& Pontici, ferocissi-
mæ gentes, illi quasi omnium fortissimo assignatę sunt. De cu-
ius morte ac filiorum eius 15. vide Justin.lib.17. Lysimachiam
condidit, quæ terræ motu corruit.
ANTIGONVS Gonatas , Demetrij Asiæ regis filius,
apud Macedones regnat anno mundi 3686. ante Christum
natum 276. Pyrrhus Antigonum fugat: Macedoniam occu-
pat:post cuius mortem Peloponnesij Antigono traduntur: tan-
dem multiplici bello pressus, in speciem castrorum parua ma-
nu adversus cæteros relicta, totis viribus in Gallos contendit,
quos vicit. Interim Alexander Rex Epiri in ultionem mortis
Pyrrhi patris sui, Macedoniam depopulatur, & capit: Deme-
trius Antigoni filius eam recipit, regnóque Epiri Alexandrum
spoliat. Cosulito Justi. lib.25.& 26. ac Plutar.in Pau.Aemi.

page.notes: The two medallions are illustrations, not running text. Left coin: a laureate head in profile facing right, with the legend LYSIMACHVS around the rim. Right coin: a helmeted head in profile facing right, with the legend ANTIGONVS partly visible, reading TI / GO / NAS and a partly legible word on the lower left. Its outer legend is not fully readable, so it is not transcribed. Ampersands are written as & in the XML. The printed text in the paragraph beginning "Thraces" is set as "Thraces,& Pontici". The word "Cosulito" is printed that way and is kept as printed.
